title: Chicken Curry with Turmeric, Cream and Lemon
description: A mild, creamy chicken curry sharpened with lemon, from Hannah Glasse's best-selling The Art of Cookery Made Plain and Easy. Glasse printed one of the first curry recipes in English; this turmeric-and-cream version appears in the book's mid-18th-century editions.
notes:
To make a Currey the Indian Way.
TAKE two small Chickens, skin them and cut them as for a Fricasey, wash them clean, and stew them in about a Quart of Water, for about five Minutes, then strain off the Liquor and put the Chickens in a clean Dish; take three large Onions, chop them small and fry them in about two Ounces of Butter, then put in the Chickens and fry them together till they are Brown, take a Quarter of an Ounce of Turmerick, a large Spoonful of Ginger and beat Pepper together, and a little Salt to your Palate, strew all these Ingredients over the Chickens whilst it is frying; then pour in the Liquor, and let it stew about Half an Hour, then put in a Quarter of a Pint of Cream, and the Juice of two Lemons, and serve it up. The Ginger, Pepper and Turmerick must be beat very fine.

Hannah Glasse, *The Art of Cookery, Made Plain and Easy* (4th edition, London, 1751), p. 101. Long s (ſ) is printed as s; OCR checked against the page scan.

Adapted: skinned bone-in thighs and drumsticks stand in for two small chickens, the "large Spoonful" of ginger and pepper is split into measured amounts, and only part of the parboiling liquor is used so the sauce ends up "pretty thick" as Glasse wanted.
ingredients: 3 pounds (1.4 kg) bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks, skin removed
steps: Put the chicken and water in a large pot, bring to a simmer, and cook for 5 minutes. Drain, reserving the liquid, and set the chicken aside on a clean plate.
Melt the butter in a wide, heavy pan over medium heat. Add the onions and cook, stirring often, until soft and golden, 12 to 15 minutes.
Add the chicken, raise the heat to medium-high, and fry, turning the pieces, until browned in patches, 8 to 10 minutes.
Mix the turmeric, ginger, pepper, and salt and sprinkle over the chicken as it fries. Stir for 1 minute, until fragrant.

Pour in 2 cups of the reserved liquid and scrape up the browned bits. Simmer gently, partly covered, until the chicken is tender and the sauce has thickened, about 30 minutes. Add a splash more liquid if it gets too thick.
Lower the heat and stir in the cream. Add the lemon juice a little at a time, tasting as you go, and warm through without boiling. Adjust the salt.
Serve with plain boiled rice on the side, as Glasse did.
